questions.question_text: Use an efficient mental method to calculate $72 \times 25$.

options.why: Treated multiplying by 25 as multiplying by 100 without taking one quarter.
Multiplied by 4 because 25 is one quarter of 100, reversing the useful relationship.
Added 25 to 1800 after the multiplication, counting the factor a second time.
Rounded 96 to 100 but did not subtract the four missing groups of 75.
Added four groups of 75 after rounding 96 up to 100 instead of subtracting them.
Subtracted only 400 from 7500, treating four groups of 75 as four groups of 100.
Halved only twice, which divides by 4 rather than dividing by 8.
Halved only once, so the calculation stopped after dividing by 2.
Partitioned as 1200 and 48 but calculated 48 divided by 8 as 8 instead of 6.
Multiplied the hundreds and tens but omitted the four ones from the partition.
Calculated 9 times 4 as 45 instead of 36 when combining the part-products.
Appended the multiplier 9 to 214 instead of multiplying each place-value part.

questions.question_text: Which result should a reliable written method give for $528 \times 34$?

options.why: Used 528 times 3 for the tens digit without shifting that partial product one place.
Included the tens partial product but omitted the product of 528 and 4.
Used one group of 528 for the ones partial product instead of four groups.
Divided by 100 but omitted the multiplication by 4 needed to replace division by 25.
Multiplied by 4 but divided by 10 rather than dividing by 100.
Divided by 4 because 25 times 4 is 100, reversing the efficient operation.
